Altitude Pressure Calculator

The barometric formula gives air pressure at any altitude (below 11,000 m) from sea-level pressure — in hPa, inHg and percent of sea level.

–
Pressure (hPa)
–
Pressure (inHg)
–
% of sea level

P = P₀ · (1 − 0.0065·h/288.15)^5.25588. Valid below 11,000 m (tropopause). Assumes the standard 6.5 °C/km lapse rate.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter the sea-level pressure (default 1013.25 hPa).
  2. Enter the altitude in metres or feet.
  3. Read the pressure at altitude in hPa, inHg and as a percent of sea level.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is the barometric formula?

P = P₀ × (1 − 0.0065·h/288.15)^5.25588, with h in metres — the standard-atmosphere barometric formula, valid below 11,000 m (the tropopause).

What sea-level pressure should I enter?

Sea-level pressure varies with weather around 1013.25 hPa (the ISA standard). Enter your local sea-level (QNH) pressure for the most accurate result.

Why is there an 11,000 m limit?

The formula assumes the standard troposphere lapse rate of 6.5 °C per km and stops being valid above the tropopause (11,000 m).
